quote: This cached thought has been around for three decades. Still no general intelligence. But, somehow, everyone outside the field knows that neural networks are the Dominant-Paradigm-Overthrowing New Idea
content: Being right about a two-word phrase is not the same as having the idea. What produced the results was a specific architecture, a specific objective, a specific scale of data and compute, and a decade of engineering that nobody outside the field had in mind when they said "neural networks"; the outsiders the essay describes could not have distinguished a convolutional network from a Hopfield net, and their prediction was compatible with every outcome. That is the essay's complaint about cached thoughts: the phrase carried no content that could have been wrong. The essay's own concession — that a cached thought can be true — applies here, and the honest verdict is that the cache was right and empty at the same time.

quote: Isn’t it funny how nonconformists all dress the same…
content: The mousetrap claim is an inference about motives and the essay marks it as a suspicion. It also has more support than the annotation allows, in the annotation's own citation: if people adopt tastes to signal group membership and abandon them when the wrong group adopts them, then the demand for an original solution is being driven by the signal value of originality rather than by the problem, which is the essay's claim about the mousetrap transposed one level (Berger & Heath 2008). The essay's conclusion — that "think outside the box" names a box — is a claim about the phrase, and it is confirmed by every list of approved unconventional answers.
